offence_severity: Life imprisonment / Rigorous imprisonment for a term of not less than ten years, and fine
physical_harm: Injuries or death caused, briefly: The court found that the prosecution failed to prove that the accused intended to cause death or that any death resulted from the act.
number_of_offences: Two offences/counts charged, one finally upheld (Section 25(1B)(a) of the Arms Act)
key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted the FSL report which indicated that the right barrel of the 12 bore gun could not be used for firing and the empty cartridges were not fired from the left barrel, thereby discrediting the use of the gun by the appellant.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the credibility of the prosecution witnesses as insufficient, noting that none of them saw the appellant firing on the police party, and that their testimonies did not conclusively establish the appellant's intention or knowledge to commit an offence. The court also noted that three independent witnesses did not support the prosecution's case.
post_offence_conduct: The accused surrendered after the firing incident and were taken into custody. The arrest and seizure were prepared at the police station and not on the spot.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 15.6.2006; Trial judgment: 7.3.2009; High Court decision: 14.02.2020; Supreme Court decision: 1.2.2022
legal_representation: H. K. Chaturvedi, Ms. Anjali Chaturvedi, Sagan Chaturvedi, Ms. Megha Chaturvedi, Advs. for the Appellant; Mukul Singh, Ankit Mishra, Gopal Jha, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: Challan filed; charges framed under Sections 307/34 IPC read with Section 3/25(1B)(a) and 27 of the Arms Act
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted; High Court: Confirmed trial court judgment and dismissed appeal; Supreme Court: Partly allowed appeal, set aside conviction and sentence for charges under Sections 307/34 IPC and 27 Arms Act, acquitted appellant except for charge under Section 25(1B)(a) of the Arms Act
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons fired at the police personnel from inside a house, leading to a retaliatory police response. The accused then surrendered with firearms, and the Trial Court convicted them under Sections 307/34 IPC and 27 of the Arms Act.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove the accused's intention or knowledge to commit an act against the police, as no witness saw the appellant firing on the police. The FSL report also cast doubt on the use of the gun seized from the appellant.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the prosecution must prove the case beyond reasonable doubt, and the conviction cannot be based on presumption to rule out the presence of the accused.
precedent_relied_upon: Parsuram Pandey 6 and others v. State of Bihar, AIR 2004 SC 5068 : [2004] 5 Suppl. SCR 475
other_sentence_order: The Court acquitted the appellant for the charges under Sections 307/34 IPC and 27 of the Arms Act, except for the charge under Section 25(1B)(a) of the Arms Act. The appellant was directed to be released forthwith from jail as he had already served the sentence for the charge under Section 25(1B)(a).
